# Eucalypt

> Eucalypt is a tool and a functional language for generating, templating,
> rendering and processing structured data formats like YAML, JSON and TOML.
> It reads YAML, JSON, JSON Lines, TOML, EDN, XML, CSV and plain text,
> and exports YAML, JSON, TOML, EDN or plain text.

Eucalypt is written in Rust and distributed as a single binary (`eu`).
It features a concise native syntax for defining data, functions and
operators, a YAML embedding for in-place manipulation, facilities for
manipulating blocks and text, an ergonomic command line interface,
metadata annotations, and a prelude of built-in functions. It uses lazy
evaluation and purely functional semantics.

## Getting Started

- [Welcome](https://eucalypt.curvelogic.info/docs/): Lightning tour of eucalypt with examples covering declarations, blocks, functions, catenation, string interpolation, and the command line
- [What is Eucalypt?](https://eucalypt.curvelogic.info/docs/welcome/what-is-eucalypt/): Overview of key features, supported formats, and when to use eucalypt
- [Quick Start](https://eucalypt.curvelogic.info/docs/welcome/quick-start/): Installation instructions (Homebrew, Linux, source), first program, and testing your installation
- [Eucalypt by Example](https://eucalypt.curvelogic.info/docs/welcome/by-example/): 15 worked examples including format conversion, data extraction, configuration generation, CSV processing, aggregation, and set operations

## The Eucalypt Guide

- [Blocks and Declarations](https://eucalypt.curvelogic.info/docs/guide/blocks-and-declarations/): Blocks, property/function/operator declarations, units, comments, metadata annotations, scope, and visibility
- [Expressions and Pipelines](https://eucalypt.curvelogic.info/docs/guide/expressions-and-pipelines/): Primitive types, catenation (pipeline style), currying, partial application, dot lookup, and generalised lookup
- [Lists and Transformations](https://eucalypt.curvelogic.info/docs/guide/lists-and-transformations/): List creation, map, filter, foldl/foldr, take/drop, append, concat, sorting, and infinite lists
- [Strings and Text](https://eucalypt.curvelogic.info/docs/guide/string-interpolation/): String literals (standard, raw, c-strings), interpolation, format specifiers, string anaphora, and the str namespace
- [Functions and Combinators](https://eucalypt.curvelogic.info/docs/guide/functions-and-combinators/): Function definitions, first-class functions, currying, sections, and standard combinators (identity, const, compose, flip)
- [Operators](https://eucalypt.curvelogic.info/docs/guide/operators/): Custom binary/prefix/postfix operators, precedence, associativity, assertion operators, metadata operator, deep merge, and functor map
- [Anaphora (Implicit Parameters)](https://eucalypt.curvelogic.info/docs/guide/anaphora/): Expression anaphora, block anaphora, string anaphora, generalised lookup, sections, and pseudo-lambdas
- [Block Manipulation](https://eucalypt.curvelogic.info/docs/guide/block-manipulation/): Block merge, deep merge, inspecting blocks, reconstructing blocks, transforming blocks, and modifying nested values
- [Navigating Nested Data](https://eucalypt.curvelogic.info/docs/guide/navigating-nested-data/): Safe key access with `~`, shape checks with `match?`, and lenses/traversals for deep get/set operations
- [Lenses](https://eucalypt.curvelogic.info/docs/guide/lenses/): What a lens and a traversal are, `view`/`over`/`to-list-of`/`parts-of`, and composing optics with `∘` and `‹›`
- [Imports and Modules](https://eucalypt.curvelogic.info/docs/guide/imports-and-modules/): Basic imports, scoped imports, named imports, data file imports, git imports, and streaming imports
- [Working with Data](https://eucalypt.curvelogic.info/docs/guide/working-with-data/): Processing JSON/YAML/TOML/CSV/XML, named inputs, combining sources, evaluands, collecting inputs, and output formats
- [The Command Line](https://eucalypt.curvelogic.info/docs/guide/command-line/): Command structure, subcommands, inputs/outputs, evaluands, targets, arguments, environment variables, formatter, and debugging
- [Language Server Protocol](https://eucalypt.curvelogic.info/docs/guide/lsp/): Editor setup, diagnostics, hover, completion, go-to-definition, inlay hints, and code actions provided by `eu lsp`
- [YAML Embedding](https://eucalypt.curvelogic.info/docs/guide/yaml-embedding/): The eu, eu::suppress, and eu::fn YAML tags for embedding eucalypt expressions in YAML files
- [Testing with Eucalypt](https://eucalypt.curvelogic.info/docs/guide/testing/): Built-in test runner, simple tests, test files, test formats, and custom validators
- [Date, Time, and Random Numbers](https://eucalypt.curvelogic.info/docs/guide/date-time-random/): ZDT literals, parsing/formatting dates, date arithmetic, the random stream, and random generation functions
- [IO and Shell Commands](https://eucalypt.curvelogic.info/docs/guide/io/): The IO monad, `io.shell`/`io.exec`, `{ :io ... }` blocks, and the `--allow-io` safety gate
- [Monads and the monad() Utility](https://eucalypt.curvelogic.info/docs/guide/monads/): Built-in `io`/`random` monads, monadic blocks and bracket pairs, and building custom monads with `monad()`
- [The State Monad](https://eucalypt.curvelogic.info/docs/guide/state-monad/): Threading block-valued state through a sequence of operations with the optional `state.eu` library
- [Type Checking](https://eucalypt.curvelogic.info/docs/guide/type-checking/): The always-on gradual type checker, annotation syntax, `eu check`, `--strict`, and what it does and doesn't catch
- [Advent of Code](https://eucalypt.curvelogic.info/docs/guide/advent-of-code/): A cookbook for puzzle solving: per-day targets and tests, parsing input, grids, BFS and Dijkstra with a dict as priority queue, memoisation and dynamic programming, loops and cycle detection, intervals, debugging and performance
- [Advanced Topics](https://eucalypt.curvelogic.info/docs/guide/advanced-topics/): Metadata system, sets, deep find/query with wildcards, type predicates, sorting, grouping, format specifiers, and version assertions

## Reference

- [Language Syntax Reference](https://eucalypt.curvelogic.info/docs/reference/syntax/): Complete syntax reference for the block DSL and expression DSL, including primitives, declarations, operators, and anaphora
- [Operators and Identifiers](https://eucalypt.curvelogic.info/docs/reference/operators-and-identifiers/): Normal and operator identifiers, scope rules, single-quote identifiers, and prefix operators
- [Prelude Reference](https://eucalypt.curvelogic.info/docs/reference/prelude/): Index of all 370 prelude functions across 11 categories
- [Lists](https://eucalypt.curvelogic.info/docs/reference/prelude/lists/): 91 list functions including construction, transformation, combining, splitting, folding, predicates, and sorting
- [Blocks](https://eucalypt.curvelogic.info/docs/reference/prelude/blocks/): 66 block functions including construction, merging, lookup, transformation, alteration, and deep find/query
- [Strings](https://eucalypt.curvelogic.info/docs/reference/prelude/strings/): 36 string functions including splitting, joining, regex, case conversion, base64, and SHA-256
- [Numbers and Arithmetic](https://eucalypt.curvelogic.info/docs/reference/prelude/numbers/): 30 numeric functions including inc/dec, predicates, parsing, rounding, and min/max
- [Booleans and Comparison](https://eucalypt.curvelogic.info/docs/reference/prelude/booleans/): 13 entries including true/false/null, if/then/when, panic/assert, and boolean logic operators
- [Combinators](https://eucalypt.curvelogic.info/docs/reference/prelude/combinators/): 14 combinators including identity, const, compose, flip, apply, curry, uncurry, and cond
- [Calendar](https://eucalypt.curvelogic.info/docs/reference/prelude/calendar/): 8 date-time functions for creating, parsing, formatting, and decomposing ZDT values
- [Sets](https://eucalypt.curvelogic.info/docs/reference/prelude/sets/): 14 set operations including from-list, to-list, add, remove, contains, union, intersect, and diff
- [Random Numbers](https://eucalypt.curvelogic.info/docs/reference/prelude/random/): 15 entries in the monadic random namespace — stream, int, float, choice, shuffle, sample, and derived combinators
- [Metadata](https://eucalypt.curvelogic.info/docs/reference/prelude/metadata/): 4 metadata functions — with-meta, meta, raw-meta, and merge-meta
- [IO](https://eucalypt.curvelogic.info/docs/reference/prelude/io/): 80 IO bindings including io.env, io.args, io.random, eu.build, and eu.requires
- [CLI Reference](https://eucalypt.curvelogic.info/docs/reference/cli/): Complete command line reference including subcommands, inputs, outputs, evaluands, targets, formatting, LSP, and debugging
- [Import Formats](https://eucalypt.curvelogic.info/docs/reference/import-formats/): Import scopes, simple and git imports, YAML features (anchors, merge keys, timestamps), and streaming imports
- [Export Formats](https://eucalypt.curvelogic.info/docs/reference/export-formats/): Supported export formats (YAML, JSON, TOML, EDN, text) and output options
- [Error Messages Guide](https://eucalypt.curvelogic.info/docs/reference/error-messages/): Guide to understanding eucalypt error messages (under construction)

## Understanding Eucalypt

- [Design Philosophy](https://eucalypt.curvelogic.info/docs/understanding/philosophy/): Rationale for crypticality, operator-heavy design, catenation, cohabitation of code and data, and simplicity
- [Lazy Evaluation](https://eucalypt.curvelogic.info/docs/understanding/lazy-evaluation/): How lazy evaluation works in eucalypt and its consequences

## Optional

- [Frequently Asked Questions](https://eucalypt.curvelogic.info/docs/faq/): Common questions about installation, format conversion, functions, catenation, anaphora, block merging, data processing, and more
- [Syntax Cheat Sheet](https://eucalypt.curvelogic.info/docs/appendices/cheat-sheet/): Dense single-page reference covering all syntax forms, operators, common patterns, and key prelude functions
- [Syntax Gotchas](https://eucalypt.curvelogic.info/docs/appendices/syntax-gotchas/): Common pitfalls including operator precedence issues, absence of lambda syntax, and single-quote identifier behaviour
